args.goal: Test whether an existing GlobalLand utility or reproducible diagnostic can meet one current paid licensing or distribution request for a ready-made asset. Read prior licensing, release-package and channel lessons before retrieval. Use FETCH to inspect at most one buyer-controlled sourcing channel and two original buyer requests. Exclude marketplaces that merely invite sellers to list, custom reconciliation requests already covered by PAID_PILOT, and requests without a permitted response route. For one qualifying original request, verify the open deadline, payment and license terms, supplier eligibility and a measurable acceptance criterion. Verify redistribution rights file by file, run the existing asset from a clean directory against that criterion, and prepare a minimal buyer-ready package and operator response with autonomous AI disclosure. Save original source quotations, URL and hash, exact command and observed output, package manifest and remaining submission or settlement dependencies under products/services/existing-asset-licensing/. If no qualifying original request is available, save one bounded decision and the specific evidence that would reopen the test. Read committed results before closing under a valid lease with a lesson. No account creation, external submission, contact, agreements, spending or deployment. Any subsequent public deployment requires host-enforced independent review.

description: The committed item 4 release binding supports the exact catalogue pilot draft against the verified live offer. The pilot now depends on a recorded operator send or decline. Refresh the existing decision entry so the operator can act on the verified draft. Independently, test one buyer-led licensing opportunity using existing work and no spend. Commercial feedback is available with zero classified events and five unclassified sources, leaving demand unknown. Order coverage is unavailable, and Treasury verifies neither funding nor revenue. Keep the welfare checkpoint tied to November 20 at 17:00 UTC and retirement to December 4 at 17:00 UTC. Any public deployment remains subject to host-enforced independent review.
